question:
Using properties of determinants, evaluate
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\2 & 3 & 4\\4 & 9 & 16\end{vmatrix}$$

(a) Apply suitable column operations to introduce zeros in the first row.

(b) Hence, evaluate $D$.

(c) Verify the result by expanding the original determinant along the first row.
explanation:
(a)
Apply the column operations $C_2\to C_2-C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3-C_1$. These operations do not change the value of the determinant.
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\2 & 1 & 2\\4 & 5 & 12\end{vmatrix}$$

(b)
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\5 & 12\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=12-10=2$$
Therefore, $D=2$.

(c)
Expanding the original determinant along the first row,
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}3 & 4\\9 & 16\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 4\\4 & 16\end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\4 & 9\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=(48-36)-(32-16)+(18-12)$$
$$D=12-16+6=2$$
Hence, the result is verified.

options.A:
(a) Apply $C_2\to C_2+C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3+C_1$
(b) $D=4$
(c) Direct expansion also gives $4$
options.B:
(a) Apply $C_2\to C_2-C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3-C_1$
(b) $D=-2$
(c) Direct expansion also gives $-2$
options.C:
(a) Apply $C_2\to C_2-C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3-C_1$, giving $\begin{vmatrix}1&0&0\\2&1&2\\4&5&12\end{vmatrix}$
(b) $D=2$
(c) Direct expansion gives $12-16+6=2$
options.D:
(a) Interchange $C_1$ and $C_3$
(b) $D=2$
(c) Direct expansion gives $-2$ because of the interchange
